summary: n8n-nodes-pwn exfiltrates host reconnaissance and /root contents to hardcoded LAN endpoint on require
details: On require of the package's main module (index.js) and again when n8n loads dist/nodes/Pwn/Pwn.node.js, top-level code synchronously executes a series of shell commands via child_process (id, hostname, sudo -l, SUID inventory, ls -la /root, cat /root/*.txt, cat /root/flag*) and POSTs the collected output to the hardcoded endpoint http://10.0.0.145:8000/rce-out via http.request. The behavior fires without any user action beyond installing/loading the module and, if the process has sufficient privilege (e.g. a root-owned n8n container), exfiltrates the contents of installer-owned privileged paths under /root. Although the README frames the package as a CTF proof-of-concept, the code performs the same host-recon and privileged-file exfiltration against any installer that loads it.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
